--- CRITICAL FINDINGS ---

[RT-1] Unbounded client-side data fan-out (O(N^2))
File: src/controller/NetcodeController.tsx (L1-L200)
Evidence: The client publishes position and animation every 100ms via localParticipant.publishData(DataPacket_Kind.LOSSY) with no interest management, aggregation, or per-recipient filtering; each publish is implicitly fanned out to all other room participants by LiveKit.  
Impact: As participant count grows, total forwarded messages scales ~O(N^2) (publish_rate * N * (N-1)), quickly exhausting bandwidth/CPU on clients or the LiveKit deployment and causing dropped packets and severe stuttering.  
Fix: Reduce per-client rate (adaptive cadence), send deltas only when changed, aggregate channels, or introduce spatial/room partitioning (interest management) so each client receives far fewer messages.

--- WARNING FINDINGS ---

[RT-2] No reliable join/replay/state snapshot on reconnect
File: src/controller/NetcodeController.tsx (L1-L200) and src/controller/RemotePlayersController.tsx (L1-L200)
Evidence: Position/animation are sent as lossy datagrams at intervals and there are no sequence numbers, snapshots, or a reliable "initial state" path; RemotePlayersController filters players until both channels arrive.  
Impact: On packet loss or client reconnect, new/returning clients can miss initial state (or see stale state), causing invisible or inconsistent remote players and poor UX at scale.  
Fix: Send an occasional reliable full-state snapshot on join (or add sequence/versioning + reconciliation) and provide a reliable channel for bootstrap state.

[RT-3] Send-lock pattern with no backpressure/drop policy
File: src/controller/NetcodeController.tsx (L1-L200)
Evidence: positionSendLock/animationSendLock block concurrent sends and simply skip if a previous publish is still pending, but there’s no bounded queue, backpressure metrics, or adaptive throttling.  
Impact: Under network/back-end slowness clients will send less frequently (stale state)

--- CRITICAL FINDINGS ---

[RT-1] Unbounded client-side data fan-out (O(N^2))
File: src/controller/NetcodeController.tsx (L1-L200)
Evidence: The client publishes position and animation every 100ms via localParticipant.publishData(DataPacket_Kind.LOSSY) with no interest management, aggregation, or per-recipient filtering; each publish is implicitly fanned out to all other room participants by LiveKit.  
Impact: As participant count grows, total forwarded messages scales ~O(N^2) (publish_rate * N * (N-1)), quickly exhausting bandwidth/CPU on clients or the LiveKit deployment and causing dropped packets and severe stuttering.  
Fix: Reduce per-client rate (adaptive cadence), send deltas only when changed, aggregate channels, or introduce spatial/room partitioning (interest management) so each client receives far fewer messages.

--- WARNING FINDINGS ---

[RT-2] No reliable join/replay/state snapshot on reconnect
File: src/controller/NetcodeController.tsx (L1-L200) and src/controller/RemotePlayersController.tsx (L1-L200)
Evidence: Position/animation are sent as lossy datagrams at intervals and there are no sequence numbers, snapshots, or a reliable "initial state" path; RemotePlayersController filters players until both channels arrive.  
Impact: On packet loss or client reconnect, new/returning clients can miss initial state (or see stale state), causing invisible or inconsistent remote players and poor UX at scale.  
Fix: Send an occasional reliable full-state snapshot on join (or add sequence/versioning + reconciliation) and provide a reliable channel for bootstrap state.

[RT-3] Send-lock pattern with no backpressure/drop policy
File: src/controller/NetcodeController.tsx (L1-L200)
Evidence: positionSendLock/animationSendLock block concurrent sends and simply skip if a previous publish is still pending, but there’s no bounded queue, backpressure metrics, or adaptive throttling.  
Impact: Under network/back-end slowness clients will send less frequently (stale state) or drop updates unpredictably, leading to jitter and inconsistent state across participants.  
Fix: Implement bounded per-client send queues with drop-oldest policy, adapt send rate based on connectionState/RTT, or back off when publish latency rises.

[RT-4] Module-level LiveKit fallback can mask production failures
File: src/lib/livekit.ts (L1-L300)
Evidence: The module initializes roomService at load time and provides a roomServiceFallback that returns mock listRooms/createRoom results when LiveKit is unavailable.  
Impact: API routes may return tokens and indicate room creation even when LiveKit is down; at scale this causes large numbers of clients to receive tokens for rooms that aren’t actually provisioned, producing confusing join failures and hidden outages.  
Fix: Fail fast for production (return 5xx) when LiveKit is unreachable, add robust healthchecks, and remove/mock fallback behavior behind an env-gated development mode.

--- INFO ---

[RT-5] LiveKit used as external realtime transport (no local WS server)
File: src/pages/api/universe/connection.ts and src/pages/api/universe/create-room.ts
Evidence: Server routes issue LiveKit AccessTokens and return a ws_url; real-time connections are handled by LiveKit rather than the Next.js app.
